title: Tuta absoluta/Phthorimaea absoluta (Tomato Leaf miner) - Kenya

Header: Tuta absoluta/Phthorimaea absoluta (Tomato Leaf miner) - Kenya

Prevention: Plant clean seedlings free from infestation of the pest.
Rotate with non-host crops such as maize, beans and cabbages.
Uproot and destroy by burning all infected crop residues.
Clean and disinfect all equipment used in transportation of tomatoes such as boxes, crates and trucks using food grade detergents and chlorine based disinfectants.
Apply balanced crop nutrition and avoid overusing nitrogen.
Monitoring: Look out for silvery-brown adult moth in the field early in the morning.
Coalesced white to cream necrotic mines on both upper and lower parts of the leaf lamina.
Green larvae with black head inside the tunnels.
Silky web produced by the larvae to fold the leaf partially protecting older larval instars.
Puncture marks on fruit calyx with dried black frass at larvae exit hole.
Monitor moth presence using pheromone traps.
Take action once you notice 2-3 moths per trap per week.
Direct Control: In greenhouses, use screen vents in roofs and sides to reduce pest migration.
Use a biopesticide, e.g. based on
Azadirachtin (Neem) based biopesticides at recommended rate.
Restrictions: Follow instructions on the product labe (dosage, timing of application, PHI, REI).
